label: copy-phase sparse conjunction of current input, current output and next output tokens
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on the original-phase or delimiter steps, and never at recall_idx 0), mostly mid-copy (recall_idx 2-5, to_go 2-6), at about 0.1% of copy steps. It prefers input tokens r/2/3/d/m/o/h, output tokens o/2/g/h/r, next outputs g/o/2/r, and previous inputs v/c/j. But each of these is a weak factor: the input-token set alone covers 96% of activations at 0.4% precision, and stacking token conditions only gets to F1 of about 0.11-0.19 (precision 6-21%, recall 18-42%). This looks like a sparse, combinatorial code over the local token context with no single coherent description. Magnitude is narrow (median 0.118, max 0.219) and I did not find what modulates it.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=r (+5.61), phase=2 & in_tok=2 (+5.11), phase=2 & in_tok=3 (+5.07), phase=2 & in_tok=d (+4.91), phase=2 & in_tok=m (+4.73), phase=2 & in_tok=o (+4.52).
